discipline_framing: The alternative-data discipline of the futures fundamental analyst — programming-driven collection and analysis of unconventional data including satellite imagery of crop fields, oil tanker tracking, and retail foot-traffic patterns, generating fundamental edge before official government reports are published
audience: Fundamental analysts of futures and derivatives markets who need working command of Python and R data skills, scraping and API acquisition, satellite and geospatial analysis, vessel and location data, signal evaluation, and the legal-ethical framework, converting unconventional data into verified fundamental edge
sources: The alternative-data industry literature (the market-taxonomy and vendor-ecosystem studies, the hedge-fund and commodity-trading adoption research, the data-economics and alpha-decay analyses)
The programming and data-science canon (the Python scientific stack tradition from pandas through scikit-learn, the R tidyverse lineage, the data-engineering pipeline literature)
The remote-sensing science tradition (the NASA and ESA satellite-program documentation, the vegetation-index and crop-yield estimation research, the SAR and thermal imaging literatures)
The maritime-analytics literature (the AIS data-system documentation, the vessel-tracking analytics research, the global-trade-flow estimation methodologies)

The geolocation and consumer-data research (the mobility-data literature from the anonymized-location tradition, the card-transaction and receipt-panel methodologies, the app-usage analytics research)

The signal-evaluation and backtesting canon (the financial-machine-learning tradition including the López de Prado lineage, the overfitting and multiple-testing research, the nowcasting literature connecting alternative data to official statistics)

The legal and ethical framework literature (the data-privacy regulation tradition from GDPR through state laws, the web-scraping case law, the insider-information and expert-network compliance literature, the AI-ethics frameworks)
pitfalls: Vendor-brochure credulity — accepting alternative-data marketing claims about coverage, accuracy, and alpha without independent backtesting against official outcomes, paying premium prices for unverified signals

Overfitting the alternative — mining noisy non-traditional datasets with enough feature freedom to manufacture spectacular backtests that collapse instantly in live trading, the multiple-testing disaster at data scale

Legal-grey-zone scraping — acquiring data through terms-of-service violations, paywall circumvention, or personal-data collection that crosses privacy regulation, building edge on foundations that litigation or enforcement can remove overnight

Pipeline-fragility blindness — depending on scraped sources and vendor feeds whose silent schema changes, coverage shifts, and outages corrupt analysis until positions built on broken data reveal the failure

Isolated-signal syndrome — treating alternative data as standalone trade generator instead of integrating it with official reports, balance sheets, and the fundamental framework where its true value as leading indicator lives
